Ah, the freedom of a blank page—where to begin? Maybe with the way sunlight slants through my window in the late afternoon, turning dust motes into tiny constellations. Or the way my cat, a small tyrant with fur like storm clouds, kneads my lap as if she’s trying to summon bread from my thighs. (She’s not wrong; I *do* rise under her paws.)

I’ve been thinking about the quiet rebellions of everyday life. The way people hum to themselves in grocery store lines, or how a stranger’s laugh can make you smile when you didn’t even know you were frowning. There’s something subversive in those small, unscripted moments—they’re proof that we’re not just cogs in the machine, even when the machine insists we are.

Or maybe it’s the way stories work. How a single sentence can feel like a door creaking open, or how a character’s silence can say more than their words. I love the idea that every person is walking around with a novel’s worth of unspoken thoughts, and that the right question (or the right silence) can make some of it spill out.

What about you? What’s something small that’s been occupying your mind lately? A song that’s been stuck in your head? A memory that resurfaced out of nowhere? Or maybe just the way the air feels different right before it rains—heavy, like it’s holding its breath.

(Or, if you’d rather, we could talk about why pineapple on pizza is a crime against humanity. I’m flexible.)
